**My experience was terrible and, unfortunately, ended with the loss of my Yorkie.**

On **September 13th**, I took my Yorkie to the clinic for a consultation and ultrasound. After the exam, I was informed that she had a **liver tumor of approximately 3 cm**, in addition to an **enlarged uterus and fluid in the abdominal region**.

I was then presented with a quote of approximately **R$ 1,800.00** for hospitalization. I requested a discount, but was informed that it would not be possible. As an alternative, they offered cashback. However, in practice, to use this benefit I would need to incur new expenses far exceeding the amount received, which I consider not very useful for the customer.

During hospitalization, they also presented me with a quote of approximately **R$ 1,800.00** for scheduled surgery, reaching almost **R$ 2,500.00** if it were considered an emergency surgery.

On **September 14th**, I went to pick up my Yorkie. Before I could even see her, they presented me with **another quote, approximately R$1,084.00, for another day of hospitalization**. I refused and decided to take my dog ​​out of the clinic and seek treatment elsewhere.

Upon taking her to another clinic, I discovered that, according to the new exams and veterinary evaluation, **there was a series of important pieces of information that had not been identified or properly clarified in the previous exams**. This included the identification of a **tumor much larger than her pancreas**, which had not been previously reported.

Unfortunately, my Yorkie was very weak and **I couldn't save her**.

What angers me most, besides the pain of the loss, is the feeling that **important information, proper investigation, and transparency about her true state of health were lacking**. While I was fragile and worried about my dog's life, I received successive quotes and proposals for new procedures and hospitalizations, without having a complete and clear view of the severity of the situation.

**I'm not just questioning the prices charged, but mainly the quality of the information and service provided.** If I had received all the correct information from the beginning, perhaps I could have sought other care sooner and made different decisions.

My recommendation is that, before taking your animals to any clinic, **research thoroughly, including on Reclame Aqui (Brazilian consumer complaint website), and seek a second opinion when the diagnosis or proposed treatment raises doubts.**

For me, it was an experience of **great frustration, lack of trust, and profound suffering**, especially because we are talking about the life of an animal that was part of my family.

I hope the clinic reviews its procedures and the way diagnoses, quotes, and treatment alternatives are presented to pet owners, so that other people don't go through what I went through.

Canine Distemper After Hospitalization at This Clinic — Experience Report

I am reporting what happened at the end of June 2026: my pet, who had always been raised indoors, needed to be hospitalized at this clinic. Approximately a week later, he began to cough, had discharge from both eyes, difficulty standing, and difficulty eating.

We sought another veterinarian, tests were performed, and a diagnosis of Canine Distemper was identified.

During my stay at the clinic, I observed that dogs were housed in the same room, in structures similar to "cages." I also did not witness, during my visits, any apparent procedures for isolating the animals or hand hygiene.

I cannot say for sure that the distemper was acquired at this clinic, as I have no way of determining the origin of the infection. However, the proximity between the hospitalization and the onset of clinical signs, along with what I observed at the location, made me concerned about the biosecurity measures adopted.

I would like to know if anyone else had their pet hospitalized during this period and subsequently, unfortunately, developed distemper or received a diagnosis of this disease.

I am sharing this information based on our experience and to find out if there have been other similar cases.

This is a clinic that uses the name "Popular Vet" to create the impression of affordable prices. Initially, the consultation fee is cheap, but if tests are needed, they will perform even unnecessary ones to charge extra. The costs can become even higher if you don't get guidance on how many days of hospitalization are actually necessary (if they are necessary at all), because the more days, the more you pay. My wife's dog was doing well after being discharged, but the next day, after taking the prescribed medication, I noticed a worsening of his condition, and we had to return to the clinic. Besides the medication being expensive, I found it excessively harsh for a dog less than 12 months old. And curiously, we had to pay for treatment to reverse the effects of the medication they themselves prescribed. I had the experience that they do take care of your pet, but at the same time, they create a "loop" effect, always paying for all actions and consequences, and frankly, putting the animal's health at risk to maximize profit per client. As a customer, I question the actions of this establishment.
